summary:
All three items are answered for development seed 1181 (seed 20261101 was not solved), and both deliverables are written and committed (328088c). Commands run and exit codes: `uv run ruff check .` exit 0; `uv run mfos gate --fast` exit 0 ("all gates passed"); `gci_study.py merge`, `pair_jobs.py cells / fitcells / assemble / job ...` (27 solves), `derive.py` and `summarize_pairs.py` all exit 0. `pkill` exited 3 and `kill` was refused by the sandbox.

(1) Six same-stratum pairs were solved at levels 0-2 (family; 2 dies per switch; 4.5 mm dies). Three are the outcome-blind "first" pairs (gen #0,#1). Three are memory-capped "fit" pairs (gen #1,#3). The cap was chosen when gen #0 at level 2 looked too big for memory; it later fitted, and the fit pairs lean toward simpler layouts. All 45 absolute Tj max values (9 layouts) converge monotonically:
- observed order 1.14-2.23;
- frozen GCI 0.057-0.327 K, candidate GCI 0.057-0.691 K; none is anywhere near 0.025 K.

Of the 30 pairwise differences, 13 oscillate (all in the fit pairs):
- frozen GCI of the difference sequence 0.003-0.082 K (9 of 30 at or below 0.025 K);
- candidate GCI 0.005-0.394 K (5 of 30);
- bound GCI_A + GCI_B 0.14-0.63 K.

One case shows the hazard: the u_shaped fit pair moves +0.348 K then -0.003 K, so its frozen GCI is 0.003 K even though each layout moved 0.24 K at the same step. That is cancellation, not convergence.

(2) The 2D strip case with the die-attach corner was compared against a 21 M-cell reference from levels 5-6-7 (re-checked against the raw JSON). Both GCI rules are non-conservative for 3 of 6 per-die values, and the two rules are identical there: the level 0-2 observed order (1.57-2.30) falls inside [1.5, 2.5], where the candidate rule does nothing, and it keeps falling toward about 1.04 as the grid is refined. The candidate is conservative where it does act, but up to 38 times too large. For differences, GCI_A + GCI_B was conservative in both strip cases; the difference of the two Richardson corrections was not.

(3) Level 2 is the finest level that fits in 16 GB: 4.7-6.5 GB peak for about 10 M active cells, and level 3 would need at least 23 GB. At level 2 the absolute Tj accuracy is about 0.06-0.7 K, so 0.025 K is out of reach. Difference accuracy of about 0.01-0.05 K is plausible but cannot be shown with an estimator proven conservative.

Limitations: one die size; the 2D strip has no 3D die corners (the 3D single-die case was not run); there is no fine reference for full 3D layouts, and the strip-to-3D error ratio is an inference. This is a research note, not evidence.
root_cause: The frozen thermal grid rule refines toward die edges but not toward the edges of copper traces on the Al2O3 ceramic or the inset backside-copper edges. Those corners have a field exponent of 0.519, so point values converge at an order of only about 1.04. As a result the level 0-2 sequence has not yet reached its asymptotic rate: the observed order from levels 0-2 (1.5-2.3) overstates the true order, and the Roache GCI (Fs 1.25 inside [1.5, 2.5]) is non-conservative for 3 of 6 per-die values that have a validated reference. The candidate rule only changes cases outside that range, so it cannot fix these. Combined with the 16 GB limit (level 2 is the ceiling), A4's 0.025 K target cannot be reached for absolute Tj under any rule examined. Sampling the maximum Tj on the surface adds a second source of irregular, oscillating behaviour, especially in differences.
evidence: Strip2d with k(T), reference from levels 5-6-7 (21.4 M cells): true level-2 errors per die 0.034-0.051 K; frozen GCI = candidate GCI for every per-die value; non-conservative for die0 centroid (0.040 vs 0.045+-0.002), die1 tj_max (0.031 vs 0.038+-0.001) and die1 centroid (0.031 vs 0.035+-0.001).

Observed order from successive triples (0-1-2 through 5-6-7) falls monotonically, e.g. die0 mean 1.68 -> 1.16 and diff_tj_mean 1.19 -> 1.06, toward 2 x 0.519 = 1.04. In the die-only strip (no Cu-on-ceramic edges) die mean and centroid stay at 1.80-1.87 and the level-2 error is 6-16 times smaller. With constant k the same drift appears, so the Picard iteration is not the cause.
Corner exponents from k1 tan(lam pi/2) + k2 tan(lam pi) = 0: 0.835 for the die attach on Cu, 0.519 for Cu on Al2O3; the equal-k limit gives 2/3, as expected.
Dev pairs, all 27 solves: energy balance <= 4e-14, linear residual <= 3e-12, Picard <= 6 iterations. 45 absolute values: observed order 1.14-2.23, frozen GCI 0.057-0.327 K, candidate 0.057-0.691 K.
30 differences: 13 oscillate; frozen GCI 0.003-0.082 K; candidate 0.005-0.394 K; GCI_A+GCI_B 0.14-0.63 K. u_shaped fit pair: 3.770 / 4.118 / 4.115 K gives frozen GCI 0.003 K.
Memory: about 10 M active cells peaked at 4.7-6.5 GB (635-888 s); 4.4-4.7 M cells at 3.2-5.7 GB. Level 3 (36-81 M cells) needs at least 23 GB.
Strip difference check: GCI_A+GCI_B 0.102 / 0.094 K vs true 0.0072 / 0.0126 K (conservative); difference of Richardson corrections 0.009 K vs 0.0126 K (non-conservative).

alternative_explanations.explanation: H1: the singular die-attach-on-Cu corner (exponent 0.835) keeps levels 0-2 from reaching the asymptotic rate.
alternative_explanations.how_to_discriminate: Strip with only die-attach corners (every substrate layer spans the outline). Ran: the observed order stays at 1.85-1.87 for mean and centroid, so H1 is not the dominant cause.

alternative_explanations.explanation: H3: Tj max is a sampled maximum whose location moves with the grid, so its order and its differences are erratic regardless of corners.
alternative_explanations.how_to_discriminate: Compare Tj max with centroid and mean in the die-only strip. Ran: centroid and mean are regular while Tj max drifts from 1.54 to 1.23 and its difference oscillates. H3 is real but secondary.

alternative_explanations.explanation: H4: Picard or linear-solver tolerance contaminates the level-to-level change d21.
alternative_explanations.how_to_discriminate: Run with constant k. Ran: the same drift appears, and the residuals (<= 3e-12) and energy balance are far below d21. Rejected.

alternative_explanations.explanation: Planning: A4 at 0.025 K was set without checking it could be reached, so even a perfect estimator could not pass it at 16 GB.
alternative_explanations.how_to_discriminate: Compare the level-2 error under the best-case estimator with 0.025 K. Even the true strip errors (0.034-0.051 K per die) exceed it, and level 3 does not fit in memory. This is a contributing cause alongside the model cause.

discriminating_tests: T1: strip2d vs strip_dieonly, sliding-triple observed order up to level 5-7 (H1 vs H2) -- run
T2: strip2d with constant k (H4) -- run
T3: Tj max vs centroid/mean in strip_dieonly (H3) -- run
Conservativeness of frozen, candidate, bare Richardson, GCI_A+GCI_B and difference-of-corrections estimators against the level 5-6-7 reference -- run
Not run: a 3D cropped-domain reference at levels 3-4 for a full layout, and a rule that also refines trace and backside edges
recommended_actions: Founder: do not adopt the candidate rule alone as the A4 correction. It is conservative where it acts but does not fix non-conservative cases whose observed order falls inside [1.5, 2.5].
Founder: decide whether to re-scope A4. For absolute Tj, level 2 can demonstrate only about 0.06-0.7 K; 0.025 K needs 2-3 more levels (64-512 times the cells).

New experiment id, if the grid rule is to be revised: refine every trace and backside-inset edge the same way as die edges, then repeat the strip T1 and a 3D cropped-domain reference before re-freezing.

For differences: do not compute the GCI from the difference sequence alone when it oscillates or when the two layouts converge at different orders. Use GCI_A + GCI_B, or require a monotone difference sequence.
Consider reporting die-mean or centroid Tj next to Tj max; they converge more regularly.
Before re-freezing any rule, run the planned 3D single-die case or a cropped 3D layout reference (levels 0-3+) to confirm the 2D strip verdicts in 3D.
